item.text: {"text":"Recent evidence supports testing SASRec’s objective before adding architectural complexity. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) combines multiple negatives with calibrated gBCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence; its authors recommend 128–256 negatives and calibration t=0.75 as practical defaults. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies sampled softmax plus revised Transformer layers as a strong configuration, although that combined result does not isolate the loss contribution. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721) approximates full CE by selecting informative high-scoring catalog subsets, reporting substantial memory savings while preserving recommendation quality. These findings motivate multi-negative sampled softmax and gBCE comparisons; they do not establish an Electronics-specific improvement.\n\nHardness needs control: unobserved high-scoring items may be potential positives. [Hard-BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) modifies the pairwise objective to reduce false-negative influence during dynamic hard sampling; its evidence concerns implicit collaborative filtering, so transfer to SASRec requires validation. A [2024 sequential-recommendation sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity trade-offs, arguing against assuming hard or popularity sampling always wins. Practical experiment proposal: compare single-negative BCE, uniform multi-negative sampled softmax, and calibrated gBCE; then test a modest random/hard mixture. Exclude padding, the current positive, and known training-history positives from negative pools, without consulting held-out interactions. History masking prevents known-positive collisions but cannot identify latent false negatives. Select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, inspect Electronics separately, and record GPU cost; improved training margins alone are insufficient evidence."}
